text.p: The following are the stories in the Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund.

- The three Baltic presidents appealed to the leaders of NATO member states to specify support for admission of the Baltic countries to NATO. They said in a joint statement they hoped negotiations with all EU candidate states will begin no later than six months after the EU intergovernmental conference.

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele demanded information on all his ministers from relevant state institutions, the ministry of justice, the state revenue service, to check whether they are in violation of the anti-corruption law.
- Minister of Transport Vilis Krishtopans denies allegations of anti-corruption law violations.

- Company register data show that six government ministers, in violation of the anti-corruption law, are members of the management of several companies, including the economy, foreign agriculture government ministers.
- Finance Minister Robert Zile will meet representatives of the World Bank on May 27 to discuss a possible $25 million loan for the development of the agricultural infrastructure.
- Parliament chairman Alfreds Chepanis met with member of the U.S. House of Representatives David Hobsson, who confirmed continued U.S. support for Latvia's integration into NATO.

- Latvian Railway's restructuring programme has been worked out with the support of EU PHARE, involving Swedish and Dutch consulting groups. The investment programm calls for investment of $349 million to 2002.
- Lukoil LKOH.RTS plans to invest 250,000 lats in second biggest Latvian insurance company, Austrumu Aliance.
- In the first quarter of 1997, the profit of the Latvian Shipping company was $3.39 million on turnover of $72 million against forecast losses of $5.50 million.
